To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the thermal transition properties of CDA g PLLA vary with the MS of graft PLLA, (2) the enthalpy relaxation of aged CDA g PLLAs proceeds more sluggishly than that of plain PLLA, (3) the crystallization kinetics of PLLA grafts in CDA g PLLas with higher MSs is retarded, and (4) the retardation of the crystallization is ascribed to the presence of the CDA grafts.
the thermal treatment of CDA g PLLA copolymers leads to the development of a supramolecular structure, and that this structure formation process is strongly influenced by the MS of lactyl unit.

the thermal treatment of cellulose diacetyl graft poly(L-lactide)s, depending on the molar ratio of the lactyl unit, induces the development of suprarmolecular structures with different morphologies, which are different from those for the homopolymer of poly(L-lactides).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of supracellular structures for a new class of biodegradable cellulose ester grafted poly(lactic acid)s.
the thermal transition and the supramolecular structure of cellulose di acetate graft poly (L-lactide)s.

the effect of thermal treatment on the development of the supramolecular structures in the series of CDA g PLLA, with a particular focus on the MS dependence of the thermodynamic and kinetic aspects of the structural development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the CDA backbone, in the case of MS>4.7, acts not only as an "anchoring substrate," but also as a "linked diluent." The "linked diluent effect," in turn, is responsible for the observed slower crystallization kinetics.
the supramolecular development for the present series of CDA g PLLA copolymers is governed mainly by the MS of lactyl unit.

the graft copolymetrs of MS=4.7 and MS=22 are characterized by a much more rigid and less mobile amorphous phase and by a much more slowly growing crystalline phase, respectively, compared with the corresponding PLLA homopolymer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the supramolecular structures of CDA g PLLA are developed through the interplay of the backbone and the graft chains, and that the backbone plays a crucial role as the "anchoring substrate," whereas the graft chains are responsible for the formation of the supramolecular structure as "linked diluent."
the CDA backbone is a good candidate to control the development of suprmolecular structures in graft copolymetrs.

the CDA g PLLA copolymer with MS = 22 77 is a promising biodegradable material, which is expected to have a high crystallinity and a slow crystallization rate, as well as a high Tg, a low water absorption, a good mechanical property and a good biocompatibility.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the graft copolymer system of CDA g PLLA provides a unique opportunity to investigate the effect of the backbone on the crystallization behavior of the PLLA graft, because of the unique characteristics of the CDA component, such as a high degree of crystallizability and a low melting point.
the thermal treatment effect on CDA g PLLA copolymers is quite different from that for PLLA homopolymer.
the graft copolymerization of lactyl unit to cellulose diacetates is a very effective way to control the thermal transition property of the resultant graft copolymer.
